**Im Soo-hyang** ([Korean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_language "Korean language"):임수향; born April 19, 1990) is a South Korean actress. She rose to fame playing leading roles in the [television series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_drama "Korean drama")_[New Tales of Gisaeng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Tales\_of\_Gisaeng "New Tales of Gisaeng")_ (2011) and _[Inspiring Generation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inspiring\_Generation "Inspiring Generation")_ (2014). After a series of supporting roles, she gained wide recognition for her performances in the campus romance _[My ID is Gangnam Beauty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My\_ID\_is\_Gangnam\_Beauty "My ID is Gangnam Beauty")_ (2018) and the smash-hit mystery drama _[Graceful Family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graceful\_Family "Graceful Family")_ (2019). She then starred in _[When I Was the Most Beautiful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/When\_I\_Was\_the\_Most\_Beautiful "When I Was the Most Beautiful")_ (2020), _[Woori the Virgin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woori\_the\_Virgin "Woori the Virgin")_ (2022), and _[Doctor Lawyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor\_Lawyer "Doctor Lawyer")_ (2022).

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Im_Soo-hyang&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Career")]

### 2011–2017: _New Tales of Gisaeng_ and diverse roles

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Im_Soo-hyang&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: 2011–2017: New Tales of Gisaeng and diverse roles")]

After making a bit-part appearance in the 2009 film _[4th Period Mystery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4th\_Period\_Mystery "4th Period Mystery")_ while she was still a student at [Chung-Ang University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chung-Ang_University "Chung-Ang University"), Im landed her [breakthrough role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breakthrough_role "Breakthrough role") when she was cast as Dan Sa-ran, a prideful, lower-middle class dancer, in the 2011 popular television series _[New Tales of Gisaeng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Tales\_of\_Gisaeng "New Tales of Gisaeng")_. Cast alongside [Sung Hoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sung_Hoon_(actor) "Sung Hoon (actor)") and [Han Hye-rin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Hye-rin "Han Hye-rin"), the series explored the premise that the [gisaeng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gisaeng "Gisaeng"), the Korean equivalent of a [geisha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geisha "Geisha") or [courtesan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Courtesan "Courtesan"), still existed in modern-day Korea.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-new-5) Im was nominated for several newcomer awards for her performance and won the [SBS Drama Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SBS_Drama_Awards "SBS Drama Awards") for Best New Star and the [Korea Drama Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korea_Drama_Awards "Korea Drama Awards") for Best New Actress.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-6) That same year, she had a prominent supporting role in _[Paradise Ranch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paradise\_Ranch "Paradise Ranch")_ and made a cameo appearance in _[Salamander Guru and The Shadows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salamander\_Guru\_and\_The\_Shadows "Salamander Guru and The Shadows")_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-ranch-7)

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/00/Im_Soo-Hyang.jpg/250px-Im_Soo-Hyang.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Im_Soo-Hyang.jpg)

Im at the _Iris II: New Generation_ press conference in 2013

To develop her range, Im increased her profile with starring roles as diverse as a feisty chairman's daughter in _[I Do, I Do](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_Do,\_I\_Do\_(TV\_series) "I Do, I Do (TV series)")_ (2012), a cool assassin in _[Iris II: New Generation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iris\_II:\_New\_Generation "Iris II: New Generation")_ (2013), the calculating stepdaughter of a high official in _[Inspiring Generation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inspiring\_Generation "Inspiring Generation")_ (2014), a college dropout in _[Five Enough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Five\_Enough "Five Enough")_ (2015) and the female antagonist in _[Blow Breeze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blow\_Breeze "Blow Breeze")_ (2015).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-iris-8)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-ins-9) In 2016, Im played the title character in the prison romance film _Eunha_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-eunha-10)

In 2017, Im was cast in the leading role of a widowed policewoman in _[Lovers in Bloom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lovers\_in\_Bloom "Lovers in Bloom")_, for which she received a [KBS Drama Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KBS_Drama_Awards "KBS Drama Awards") for Best Actress in a Daily Drama.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-lovers-11) Also that year, she made a cameo appearance as a serial killer who pretends to be a victim in tvN's crime procedural drama _[Criminal Minds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Criminal\_Minds\_(South\_Korean\_TV\_series) "Criminal Minds (South Korean TV series)")_, based on the [American series of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Criminal_Minds "Criminal Minds").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-criminal-12)

### 2018–present: _My ID is Gangnam Beauty_ and rising popularity

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Im_Soo-hyang&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2018–present: My ID is Gangnam Beauty and rising popularity")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7a/Lim_Soo-hyang_at_Oct_2018.png/250px-Lim_Soo-hyang_at_Oct_2018.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lim_Soo-hyang_at_Oct_2018.png)

Im at the [Atelier Cologne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atelier_Cologne "Atelier Cologne") photo call event in 2018

In 2018, Im rose in popularity when she starred opposite [Cha Eun-woo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cha_Eun-woo "Cha Eun-woo") of [Astro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astro_(South_Korean_band) "Astro (South Korean band)") in the [JTBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JTBC "JTBC") romantic comedy series _[Gangnam Beauty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gangnam\_Beauty "Gangnam Beauty")_. For her performance as Kang Mi-rae, Im won the Top Excellence Award for Actress in a Drama at the 26th Korea Culture and Entertainment Awards.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-13)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-14)

In 2019, Im received critical acclaim for her portrayal of Mo Seok-hee, a confident, charismatic and savage [chaebol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaebol "Chaebol") heiress, in the mystery drama _[Graceful Family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graceful\_Family "Graceful Family")_. The series premiered with high viewership ratings for [MBN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maeil_Broadcasting_Network "Maeil Broadcasting Network") network and attracted media attention in Korea and internationally.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-15)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-grace-16) In 2020, Im next starred in the romance melodrama _[When I Was the Most Beautiful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/When\_I\_Was\_the\_Most\_Beautiful "When I Was the Most Beautiful")_ opposite [Ji Soo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ji_Soo "Ji Soo") and [Ha Seok-jin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ha_Seok-jin "Ha Seok-jin"), portraying an optimistic ceramic artist who falls in love with two brothers. Im was again praised for her acting and she went on to gain the Top Excellence prize at the 39th [MBC Drama Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MBC_Drama_Awards "MBC Drama Awards").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-MBC2020-17)

In 2022, she played the titular role of Oh Woo-ri in the [SBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seoul_Broadcasting_System "Seoul Broadcasting System")[romantic comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romantic_comedy "Romantic comedy") drama _[Woori the Virgin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woori\_the\_Virgin "Woori the Virgin")_ based on American series _[Jane the Virgin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jane\_the\_Virgin "Jane the Virgin")_, reuniting with _[New Tales of Gisaeng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Tales\_of\_Gisaeng "New Tales of Gisaeng")_ co-star [Sung Hoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sung_Hoon_(actor) "Sung Hoon (actor)").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-18) The same year she starred in the [MBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munhwa_Broadcasting_Corporation "Munhwa Broadcasting Corporation")[medical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_drama "Medical drama")-[legal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legal_drama "Legal drama") drama _[Doctor Lawyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor\_Lawyer "Doctor Lawyer")_ in the role of a prosecutor.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-19) Later in July, Im joined the 'Bubble for Actors' platform.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-20)

In 2023, she played the role of Han Gye-jeol in the MBC romantic fantasy drama _[Kokdu: Season of Deity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kokdu:\_Season\_of\_Deity "Kokdu: Season of Deity")_ opposite [Kim Jung-hyun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kim_Jung-hyun_(actor,_born_1990) "Kim Jung-hyun (actor, born 1990)") portraying an [ER doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emergency_physician "Emergency physician") who graduated from the lowest-ranking medical school in the country.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-21) In 2024, she played the role of Park Do-ra in the [KBS2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KBS2 "KBS2") drama _[Beauty and Mr. Romantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beauty\_and\_Mr.\_Romantic "Beauty and Mr. Romantic")_ opposite [Ji Hyun-woo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ji_Hyun-woo "Ji Hyun-woo").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-22)

**Im Soo-hyang** ([Korean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_language "Korean language"):임수향; born April 19, 1990) is a South Korean actress. She rose to fame playing leading roles in the [television series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_drama "Korean drama")_[New Tales of Gisaeng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Tales\_of\_Gisaeng "New Tales of Gisaeng")_ (2011) and _[Inspiring Generation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inspiring\_Generation "Inspiring Generation")_ (2014). After a series of supporting roles, she gained wide recognition for her performances in the campus romance _[My ID is Gangnam Beauty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My\_ID\_is\_Gangnam\_Beauty "My ID is Gangnam Beauty")_ (2018) and the smash-hit mystery drama _[Graceful Family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graceful\_Family "Graceful Family")_ (2019). She then starred in _[When I Was the Most Beautiful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/When\_I\_Was\_the\_Most\_Beautiful "When I Was the Most Beautiful")_ (2020), _[Woori the Virgin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woori\_the\_Virgin "Woori the Virgin")_ (2022), and _[Doctor Lawyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor\_Lawyer "Doctor Lawyer")_ (2022).

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Im_Soo-hyang&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Career")]

### 2011–2017: _New Tales of Gisaeng_ and diverse roles

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Im_Soo-hyang&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: 2011–2017: New Tales of Gisaeng and diverse roles")]

After making a bit-part appearance in the 2009 film _[4th Period Mystery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4th\_Period\_Mystery "4th Period Mystery")_ while she was still a student at [Chung-Ang University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chung-Ang_University "Chung-Ang University"), Im landed her [breakthrough role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breakthrough_role "Breakthrough role") when she was cast as Dan Sa-ran, a prideful, lower-middle class dancer, in the 2011 popular television series _[New Tales of Gisaeng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Tales\_of\_Gisaeng "New Tales of Gisaeng")_. Cast alongside [Sung Hoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sung_Hoon_(actor) "Sung Hoon (actor)") and [Han Hye-rin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Hye-rin "Han Hye-rin"), the series explored the premise that the [gisaeng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gisaeng "Gisaeng"), the Korean equivalent of a [geisha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geisha "Geisha") or [courtesan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Courtesan "Courtesan"), still existed in modern-day Korea.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-new-5) Im was nominated for several newcomer awards for her performance and won the [SBS Drama Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SBS_Drama_Awards "SBS Drama Awards") for Best New Star and the [Korea Drama Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korea_Drama_Awards "Korea Drama Awards") for Best New Actress.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-6) That same year, she had a prominent supporting role in _[Paradise Ranch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paradise\_Ranch "Paradise Ranch")_ and made a cameo appearance in _[Salamander Guru and The Shadows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salamander\_Guru\_and\_The\_Shadows "Salamander Guru and The Shadows")_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-ranch-7)

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/00/Im_Soo-Hyang.jpg/250px-Im_Soo-Hyang.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Im_Soo-Hyang.jpg)

Im at the _Iris II: New Generation_ press conference in 2013

To develop her range, Im increased her profile with starring roles as diverse as a feisty chairman's daughter in _[I Do, I Do](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_Do,\_I\_Do\_(TV\_series) "I Do, I Do (TV series)")_ (2012), a cool assassin in _[Iris II: New Generation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iris\_II:\_New\_Generation "Iris II: New Generation")_ (2013), the calculating stepdaughter of a high official in _[Inspiring Generation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inspiring\_Generation "Inspiring Generation")_ (2014), a college dropout in _[Five Enough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Five\_Enough "Five Enough")_ (2015) and the female antagonist in _[Blow Breeze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blow\_Breeze "Blow Breeze")_ (2015).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-iris-8)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-ins-9) In 2016, Im played the title character in the prison romance film _Eunha_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-eunha-10)

In 2017, Im was cast in the leading role of a widowed policewoman in _[Lovers in Bloom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lovers\_in\_Bloom "Lovers in Bloom")_, for which she received a [KBS Drama Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KBS_Drama_Awards "KBS Drama Awards") for Best Actress in a Daily Drama.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-lovers-11) Also that year, she made a cameo appearance as a serial killer who pretends to be a victim in tvN's crime procedural drama _[Criminal Minds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Criminal\_Minds\_(South\_Korean\_TV\_series) "Criminal Minds (South Korean TV series)")_, based on the [American series of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Criminal_Minds "Criminal Minds").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-criminal-12)

### 2018–present: _My ID is Gangnam Beauty_ and rising popularity

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Im_Soo-hyang&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2018–present: My ID is Gangnam Beauty and rising popularity")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7a/Lim_Soo-hyang_at_Oct_2018.png/250px-Lim_Soo-hyang_at_Oct_2018.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lim_Soo-hyang_at_Oct_2018.png)

Im at the [Atelier Cologne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atelier_Cologne "Atelier Cologne") photo call event in 2018

In 2018, Im rose in popularity when she starred opposite [Cha Eun-woo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cha_Eun-woo "Cha Eun-woo") of [Astro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astro_(South_Korean_band) "Astro (South Korean band)") in the [JTBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JTBC "JTBC") romantic comedy series _[Gangnam Beauty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gangnam\_Beauty "Gangnam Beauty")_. For her performance as Kang Mi-rae, Im won the Top Excellence Award for Actress in a Drama at the 26th Korea Culture and Entertainment Awards.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-13)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-14)

In 2019, Im received critical acclaim for her portrayal of Mo Seok-hee, a confident, charismatic and savage [chaebol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaebol "Chaebol") heiress, in the mystery drama _[Graceful Family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graceful\_Family "Graceful Family")_. The series premiered with high viewership ratings for [MBN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maeil_Broadcasting_Network "Maeil Broadcasting Network") network and attracted media attention in Korea and internationally.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-15)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-grace-16) In 2020, Im next starred in the romance melodrama _[When I Was the Most Beautiful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/When\_I\_Was\_the\_Most\_Beautiful "When I Was the Most Beautiful")_ opposite [Ji Soo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ji_Soo "Ji Soo") and [Ha Seok-jin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ha_Seok-jin "Ha Seok-jin"), portraying an optimistic ceramic artist who falls in love with two brothers. Im was again praised for her acting and she went on to gain the Top Excellence prize at the 39th [MBC Drama Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MBC_Drama_Awards "MBC Drama Awards").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-MBC2020-17)

In 2022, she played the titular role of Oh Woo-ri in the [SBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seoul_Broadcasting_System "Seoul Broadcasting System")[romantic comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romantic_comedy "Romantic comedy") drama _[Woori the Virgin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woori\_the\_Virgin "Woori the Virgin")_ based on American series _[Jane the Virgin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jane\_the\_Virgin "Jane the Virgin")_, reuniting with _[New Tales of Gisaeng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Tales\_of\_Gisaeng "New Tales of Gisaeng")_ co-star [Sung Hoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sung_Hoon_(actor) "Sung Hoon (actor)").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-18) The same year she starred in the [MBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munhwa_Broadcasting_Corporation "Munhwa Broadcasting Corporation")[medical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_drama "Medical drama")-[legal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legal_drama "Legal drama") drama _[Doctor Lawyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor\_Lawyer "Doctor Lawyer")_ in the role of a prosecutor.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-19) Later in July, Im joined the 'Bubble for Actors' platform.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-20)

In 2023, she played the role of Han Gye-jeol in the MBC romantic fantasy drama _[Kokdu: Season of Deity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kokdu:\_Season\_of\_Deity "Kokdu: Season of Deity")_ opposite [Kim Jung-hyun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kim_Jung-hyun_(actor,_born_1990) "Kim Jung-hyun (actor, born 1990)") portraying an [ER doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emergency_physician "Emergency physician") who graduated from the lowest-ranking medical school in the country.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-21) In 2024, she played the role of Park Do-ra in the [KBS2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KBS2 "KBS2") drama _[Beauty and Mr. Romantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beauty\_and\_Mr.\_Romantic "Beauty and Mr. Romantic")_ opposite [Ji Hyun-woo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ji_Hyun-woo "Ji Hyun-woo").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Im_Soo-hyang#cite_note-22)

_**Graceful Family**_ ([Korean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_language "Korean language"): 우아한 가; [RR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revised_Romanization_of_Korean "Revised Romanization of Korean"): _Uahan ga_) is a 2019 [South Korean television series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_drama "Korean drama") starring Im Soo-hyang, [Lee Jang-woo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Jang-woo "Lee Jang-woo"), and [Bae Jong-ok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bae_Jong-ok "Bae Jong-ok"). It aired on Wednesdays and Thursdays at 23:00 ([KST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_in_South_Korea "Time in South Korea")) of [MBN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maeil_Broadcasting_Network "Maeil Broadcasting Network") and Dramax from August 21 to October 17, 2019.

Besides receiving critical acclaim, _Graceful Family_ became the highest-rated drama in MBN network history at the time of its run, and currently is ranked as the [second-highest rated drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_drama#List_of_highest-rated_series_on_cable_television "Korean drama") of the network, after being surpassed by _[Bossam: Steal the Fate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bossam:\_Steal\_the\_Fate "Bossam: Steal the Fate")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graceful_Family#cite_note-1)

## Synopsis

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Graceful_Family&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Synopsis")]

Mo Seok-hee (Im Soo-hyang) is the only daughter of the MC Group, a large [chaebol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaebol "Chaebol") (conglomerate). Her grandfather is the founder and majority shareholder of the chaebol and her father, Mo Cheol-hee, is the President. 15 years ago, as a young teenager, Seok-hee was forced by her father to move to the United States after her mother was murdered.

Now, 15 years later, Seok-hee has become a beautiful and intelligent woman with a strong personality. She acts tough and arrogant, but hides her kindness and suffering over her mother's death. She comes back to Korea after learning that her grandfather is in a coma and is hospitalized in Seoul in a facility owned by MC Group, evading her family's efforts to prevent her return.

Heo Yoon-do ([Lee Jang-woo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Jang-woo "Lee Jang-woo")) is a lawyer with no office and only a few small clients. He works by helping the residents of his neighborhood in a makeshift office at his adoptive father's restaurant. He is diligent and ethical.

Driving from the airport, Seok-hee meets Yoon-do at a police station. After a prickly first meeting, Seok-hee sees something in Yoon-do and hires him as her lawyer, and he starts working for the TOP Team at MC Group. She finds the Mo family dysfunctional, with the President's second wife (previously his mistress) jockeying for a position with his latest mistress, a popular but fading actress (and their young son) all living in the family compound. Also living in the compound are two sons with the second wife, the older one, Mo Wan-soo, an unsuccessful film director, more interested in fast cars and wine, and the younger one, Mo Wan-joon, who is being groomed as the eventual successor, secretly hiding his transgender identity and abusing his wife (their marriage is only for show and has remained unconsummated).

The TOP Team manages the affairs of the Mo family. The TOP Team is led by Han Je-gook ([Bae Jong-ok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bae_Jong-ok "Bae Jong-ok")), a former judge who had previously been known to be fair and incorruptible. However, many years ago, after ruling against the MC Group in a case, in retaliation she was transferred to a court in a rural area. Disappointed, she agreed to work for the MC Group. Je-kook becomes an ambitious and treacherous woman who wants to control MC Group and exercise extensive influence over South Korean politics and business. At TOP, Je-kook works to cover up immoral or illegal (or in the case of the transgender son, simply embarrassing) behavior by the Mo family, and uncover the immoral and illegal secrets of powerful and wealthy Korean people, to blackmail or destroy them.

Coincidentally, Seok-hee and Yoon-do discover that they have a connection. Yoon-do's mother, a housekeeper for the Mo family 15 years ago, had been convicted of murdering Seok-hee's mother. Convinced that Yoon-do's mother was framed, they join forces to reveal the truth behind Seok-hee's mother's death, and the secrets that Je-kook and TOP hide as well as to help Seok-hee gain her rightful place in MC Group. They are helped by an editor and a reporter of a small newspaper and a friendly police officer but must struggle against the power and long reach of TOP. Along the way to seek justice, the group finds allies from the most unexpected places.

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Graceful_Family&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Reception")]

_Graceful Family_ premiered with high viewership for MBN network and attracted media attention in Korea and internationally. The [Maeil Business Newspaper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maeil_Business_Newspaper "Maeil Business Newspaper") reported the drama was sold to broadcasters in Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Thailand, Vietnam, Myanmar and North and South America due to the quality performances of its actors and actresses, script and production of the drama.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graceful_Family#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graceful_Family#cite_note-3)

_**Graceful Family**_ ([Korean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_language "Korean language"): 우아한 가; [RR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revised_Romanization_of_Korean "Revised Romanization of Korean"): _Uahan ga_) is a 2019 [South Korean television series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_drama "Korean drama") starring Im Soo-hyang, [Lee Jang-woo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Jang-woo "Lee Jang-woo"), and [Bae Jong-ok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bae_Jong-ok "Bae Jong-ok"). It aired on Wednesdays and Thursdays at 23:00 ([KST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_in_South_Korea "Time in South Korea")) of [MBN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maeil_Broadcasting_Network "Maeil Broadcasting Network") and Dramax from August 21 to October 17, 2019.

Besides receiving critical acclaim, _Graceful Family_ became the highest-rated drama in MBN network history at the time of its run, and currently is ranked as the [second-highest rated drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_drama#List_of_highest-rated_series_on_cable_television "Korean drama") of the network, after being surpassed by _[Bossam: Steal the Fate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bossam:\_Steal\_the\_Fate "Bossam: Steal the Fate")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graceful_Family#cite_note-1)

## Synopsis

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Graceful_Family&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Synopsis")]

Mo Seok-hee (Im Soo-hyang) is the only daughter of the MC Group, a large [chaebol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaebol "Chaebol") (conglomerate). Her grandfather is the founder and majority shareholder of the chaebol and her father, Mo Cheol-hee, is the President. 15 years ago, as a young teenager, Seok-hee was forced by her father to move to the United States after her mother was murdered.

Now, 15 years later, Seok-hee has become a beautiful and intelligent woman with a strong personality. She acts tough and arrogant, but hides her kindness and suffering over her mother's death. She comes back to Korea after learning that her grandfather is in a coma and is hospitalized in Seoul in a facility owned by MC Group, evading her family's efforts to prevent her return.

Heo Yoon-do ([Lee Jang-woo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Jang-woo "Lee Jang-woo")) is a lawyer with no office and only a few small clients. He works by helping the residents of his neighborhood in a makeshift office at his adoptive father's restaurant. He is diligent and ethical.

Driving from the airport, Seok-hee meets Yoon-do at a police station. After a prickly first meeting, Seok-hee sees something in Yoon-do and hires him as her lawyer, and he starts working for the TOP Team at MC Group. She finds the Mo family dysfunctional, with the President's second wife (previously his mistress) jockeying for a position with his latest mistress, a popular but fading actress (and their young son) all living in the family compound. Also living in the compound are two sons with the second wife, the older one, Mo Wan-soo, an unsuccessful film director, more interested in fast cars and wine, and the younger one, Mo Wan-joon, who is being groomed as the eventual successor, secretly hiding his transgender identity and abusing his wife (their marriage is only for show and has remained unconsummated).

The TOP Team manages the affairs of the Mo family. The TOP Team is led by Han Je-gook ([Bae Jong-ok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bae_Jong-ok "Bae Jong-ok")), a former judge who had previously been known to be fair and incorruptible. However, many years ago, after ruling against the MC Group in a case, in retaliation she was transferred to a court in a rural area. Disappointed, she agreed to work for the MC Group. Je-kook becomes an ambitious and treacherous woman who wants to control MC Group and exercise extensive influence over South Korean politics and business. At TOP, Je-kook works to cover up immoral or illegal (or in the case of the transgender son, simply embarrassing) behavior by the Mo family, and uncover the immoral and illegal secrets of powerful and wealthy Korean people, to blackmail or destroy them.

Coincidentally, Seok-hee and Yoon-do discover that they have a connection. Yoon-do's mother, a housekeeper for the Mo family 15 years ago, had been convicted of murdering Seok-hee's mother. Convinced that Yoon-do's mother was framed, they join forces to reveal the truth behind Seok-hee's mother's death, and the secrets that Je-kook and TOP hide as well as to help Seok-hee gain her rightful place in MC Group. They are helped by an editor and a reporter of a small newspaper and a friendly police officer but must struggle against the power and long reach of TOP. Along the way to seek justice, the group finds allies from the most unexpected places.

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Graceful_Family&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Reception")]

_Graceful Family_ premiered with high viewership for MBN network and attracted media attention in Korea and internationally. The [Maeil Business Newspaper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maeil_Business_Newspaper "Maeil Business Newspaper") reported the drama was sold to broadcasters in Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Thailand, Vietnam, Myanmar and North and South America due to the quality performances of its actors and actresses, script and production of the drama.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graceful_Family#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graceful_Family#cite_note-3)

**Lee Jang-woo** ([Korean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_language "Korean language"):이장우; born June 1, 1986) is a South Korean actor and singer. He is best known for his roles in the television series _[Glory Jane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glory\_Jane "Glory Jane")_, _[I Do, I Do](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_Do,\_I\_Do\_(TV\_series) "I Do, I Do (TV series)")_, _[My Only One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My\_Only\_One\_(TV\_series) "My Only One (TV series)")_ and _[Homemade Love Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homemade\_Love\_Story "Homemade Love Story")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Jang-woo#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Jang-woo#cite_note-2) Lee also became popular after being paired with [Hahm Eun-jung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hahm_Eun-jung "Hahm Eun-jung") in the [third season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Got_Married_season_3 "We Got Married season 3") of fictional marriage reality show _[We Got Married](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We\_Got\_Married "We Got Married")_.

In 2009, Lee, [No Min-woo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Min-woo "No Min-woo"), and [Hyun Woo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyun_Woo "Hyun Woo") formed the [K-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-pop "K-pop") project group 24/7, which has since disbanded after releasing the single "24 Hours a Day, 7 Days a Week". Lee also appeared in a 2011 music video for his cousin, singer [Hwanhee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hwanhee "Hwanhee").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Jang-woo#cite_note-3)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Lee_Jang-woo&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Personal life")]

On June 22, 2023, it was confirmed that Lee was in a relationship with actress Jo Hye-won.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Jang-woo#cite_note-4) On June 21, 2025, Hunus Entertainment confirmed that the couple would be getting married in November.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Jang-woo#cite_note-5) Lee and Jo married on November 23, 2025.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Jang-woo#cite_note-6)

**Lee Jang-woo** ([Korean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_language "Korean language"):이장우; born June 1, 1986) is a South Korean actor and singer. He is best known for his roles in the television series _[Glory Jane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glory\_Jane "Glory Jane")_, _[I Do, I Do](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_Do,\_I\_Do\_(TV\_series) "I Do, I Do (TV series)")_, _[My Only One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My\_Only\_One\_(TV\_series) "My Only One (TV series)")_ and _[Homemade Love Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homemade\_Love\_Story "Homemade Love Story")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Jang-woo#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Jang-woo#cite_note-2) Lee also became popular after being paired with [Hahm Eun-jung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hahm_Eun-jung "Hahm Eun-jung") in the [third season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Got_Married_season_3 "We Got Married season 3") of fictional marriage reality show _[We Got Married](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We\_Got\_Married "We Got Married")_.

In 2009, Lee, [No Min-woo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Min-woo "No Min-woo"), and [Hyun Woo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyun_Woo "Hyun Woo") formed the [K-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-pop "K-pop") project group 24/7, which has since disbanded after releasing the single "24 Hours a Day, 7 Days a Week". Lee also appeared in a 2011 music video for his cousin, singer [Hwanhee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hwanhee "Hwanhee").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Jang-woo#cite_note-3)

On June 22, 2023, it was confirmed that Lee was in a relationship with actress Jo Hye-won.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Jang-woo#cite_note-4) On June 21, 2025, Hunus Entertainment confirmed that the couple would be getting married in November.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Jang-woo#cite_note-5) Lee and Jo married on November 23, 2025.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Jang-woo#cite_note-6)
